# 00 — Setup, Toolchain & First Program

## What is this?
Welcome to C++! C++ is a high-performance, multi-paradigm systems programming language offering object-oriented programming, generic templates, low-level memory control, and zero-cost abstractions. In this introductory module, you will verify your C++ compiler toolchain and run your first compiled C++ binary.

## Why does C++ have it?
- C++ compiles directly to machine code using modern optimizing compilers (GCC, Clang, MSVC).
- The standard input/output stream library `<iostream>` provides type-safe stream operations via `std::cout` and `std::cin` without brittle format specifiers.

## Minimal Anatomy of a C++ Program
Examine `main.cpp`:

```cpp
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    std::cout << "Hello, World!\n";
    return 0;
}
```

## How to Compile and Run
Open your terminal in this directory and execute:

### 1. Compile the program using G++
```bash
g++ -Wall -Wextra -std=c++17 main.cpp -o main.exe
```

### 2. Run the compiled executable
On Windows:
```bash
.\main.exe
```
On Linux / macOS:
```bash
./main
```

### 3. Verify compiler installation
```bash
g++ --version
```

## Common Mistakes
1. Forgetting the `std::` namespace prefix when using `cout` or `endl`.
2. Omitting `#include <iostream>`.
